newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares soar to hit new record high again.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares soar to hit new record high again.

text.p: Danish share prices ended higher on Monday hitting a new record closing high, fuelled by banks but with dealers seeing possible falls looming ahead.

"Top banks climbed on fresh market rumours of a Unidanmark merger with Sweden's Nordbanken after the latter's attempt to merge with S-E-Banken failed. Falls could be ahead as the index will have trouble jumping the psychological barrier of 150 points", one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index finished 2.08 point up at a new record closing high of 149.96. The KFX March future rose 1.70 point to 148.70 with 130 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Dealers feared that the early Dow falls on Wall Street might, if they continued, trigger declines on the Danish market on Tuesday.
Unidanmark rose nine points to finish at 349, while rival Den Danske Bank put on 14 crowns to 531, fuelling the general market upsurge.
East Asiatic closed three crowns higher after announcing the sale of a loss-making meat processing plant in Germany as part of a major divestment and restructuring plan.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.401 billion crowns.
